memory_candidates.content: Before migrating N files that a duplicate-block measurement tool flagged as 'peers' onto one shared helper, re-read each file's actual wrapper/skeleton content directly rather than trusting the shape-level peer count: a shared-skeleton guard (fast-path/slow-path split) can wrap a materially DIFFERENT pattern-matching contract per file (different pattern sets, different matching semantics between a whole-path glob and a basename-only find -name), and forcing such files through a single-pattern-set shared function risks a silent finding-set/behavior change. Two of four 'remaining wrapper-carrying lints' named by a prior dispatch turned out to be this case; recorded as reasoned exclusions with a full evidence trail instead of blindly executing the literal task list.

A shared corpus-scan fast-path helper's guard condition can accommodate two different callers' conventions in one function rather than forcing a uniform call shape: one set of callers pre-populates SCAN_PATHS=(DEFAULT_SCAN) before checking eligibility (triggers on `#scan_paths==1 && scan_paths[0]==default`), while another leaves SCAN_PATHS empty and has no DEFAULT_SCAN concept at all (triggers on `#scan_paths==0`). Widening the guard to `(scan_paths==0 || (scan_paths==1 && scan_paths[0]==default)) && corpus_available` serves both without an interface change, as long as callers using the empty-array convention only invoke the function from inside their own pre-check of the fast-path precondition (never unconditionally), since the function's own slow-path fallback cannot safely substitute for a caller-specific non-find enumeration strategy.
